sections.title: 1.1 Purpose
sections.text_preview: This document describes the requirements for the Triangulation Games software.

sections.title: 1.2 Document Conventions
sections.text_preview: All the references in this document have been made by using running numeration. When you see a number between closures, example [1] this means that it refers to the first reference mentioned in the re

sections.title: 1.3 Intended Audience and Reading Suggestions
sections.text_preview: The document is meant for the software project group and also for the client to specify what will be implemented in the Triangulation Games software.

sections.title: 1.4 Project Scope
sections.text_preview: Triangulation Games software is an application that makes it possible to play various different combinatorial games as solitaire, against the computer’s AI or with another player. The system also func

sections.title: 2.1 Product Perspective
sections.text_preview: Triangular Games is a stand-alone software application that is meant to realize games described in the article “Games on Triangulations” [1].

sections.title: 2.2 Product Features
sections.text_preview: The software makes it possible to play multiple triangulation games (see [1], for more information on triangular games). The games may be played alone or against another person, depending on the type

sections.text_preview:
The system has an easy to use graphical user interface which supports both a mouse and a keyboard.

This feature is essential for the system.

sections.title: 3.4 Players can be both a Human or a Computer
3.4.1 Description and Priority
sections.text_preview:
When starting a game, the user must be able to select in between Human or Artificial Intelligence for playing a game.

This feature is of a medium priority.

3.5.1 Description and Priority
sections.text_preview:
A random artificial intelligence plays a game by choosing at random one of the legal movements at any moment in the game. Having a random artificial intelligence is must for the system.

sections.title: 3.6 The user can change the nature of players during a game
3.6.1 Description and Priority
sections.text_preview:
While playing, the user can change the nature of the players in the game, without the need of a restart. The game continues with the new selection of players.

This feature has a medium priority.

sections.title: 4.2 Hardware Interfaces
sections.text_preview: HI-1: The system functions on a computer that has a screen for output and keyboard or mouse or both for input.

sections.title: 4.3 Software Interfaces
sections.text_preview: SI-1: The system requires a working Java-environment [2] and a graphical user interface supported by the Java Swing library [4].

sections.title: 5.1 Performance Requirements
sections.text_preview:
PR-1: The system should be executed without problems in a machine that fulfills the requirements of the Java runtime environment [2].

PR-2: The basic artificial intelligence must operate fast enough.

sections.title: 5.2 Safety Requirements
sections.text_preview: The system does not use or receive network connections and is used locally. This means that no network safety requirements exist. Overwriting an existing file on the file system has to be confirmed fr

sections.title: 5.3 Security Requirements
sections.text_preview: No personal information is stored by the system so no specific security requirements need to be defined.

sections.title: 5.4 Software Quality Attributes
sections.text_preview:
The system is playable with the minimum setup defined earlier in Hardware Requirements.

SQA-1: The system shall run well on both Linux and Windows and should be playable with the mouse or the keyboar
